player.seasonOutlook: Ouzts was selected by the Seahawks in the fifth round of April's draft. The heaviest FB/TE in this class (274 pounds), Ouzts primarily worked as a blocker and his 3% target share last season limited him to 108 yards on 10 targets. He's unlikely to ever see enough targets to find his way to fantasy relevance, especially considering he's expected to focus on fullback duties in Seattle.

Allen was selected by the Jaguars in the seventh round of April's draft. His rushing efficiency at Syracuse is concerning (class-low 4.5 YPC), but he has the biggest hands in this RB class and his 83 targets and 64 receptions last season were tops in this RB class. He'll look to carve out a third-down role in the pros, but it may take a while, as Travis Etienne Jr., Tank Bigsby and fourth-round rookie Bhayshul Tuten top the Jacksonville depth chart.

Wester was selected by the Ravens in the sixth round of April's draft. He is one of the smallest WRs in this class (5-foot-9, 163 pounds), but he was productive at FAU and Colorado. He hauled in a class-high 326 receptions and 31 TD catches while also posting a class-low 11.1 YPR during his collegiate tenure (58 games). He aligned in the slot 80% of the time and also contributed as a kick and punt returner. Wester underwhelmed with a 4.46 40-yard dash at 163 pounds (82 speed score) at the combine. He's well off the fantasy radar as a returner and depth piece in a deep Ravens WR room.
